findings.problem: Unconditional root-removal after hooks are not joined to outstanding operations on test timeout. Capture creates never-aborted per-invocation signals; capability runtime shutdown only owns directCommand and cannot cancel cluster invokes. Production test stops runtime only in its body finally; an expired node:test timeout can run root-removal teardown before that async body finishes. This can delete API/state/provider files while real child/service work still runs, and generate secondary failures instead of preserving decisive evidence.
findings.required: Tie invocation cancellation to owned/test abort; track outstanding invocation/gate work and service lifetime; order teardown as cancellation, bounded awaited settlement/actual shutdown, then remove owned files. On unconfirmed termination retain files and fail explicitly. Cover partial setup/start failures. Do not use a deadline relaxation or command mock as a repair.
